title: Verify a first-time anonymous user is presented with the guided questionnaire upon visiting the home page
description: This test verifies that the primary entry point for the new preference-based onboarding flow is correctly triggered for new, anonymous users. Failure of this test would mean the entire feature is inaccessible to its target audience.
testDescription: A user who has never visited the site before, or has cleared their browser data, lands on the homepage and should immediately be presented with the guided questionnaire to capture their job preferences without needing to register or log in.
prerequisites:
1. The user must be treated as a new visitor (no existing session cookies or local storage for the site).
2. The guided questionnaire feature is enabled on the target environment.
3. The test is performed on a browser that has not visited the site before, or has had its cache and cookies cleared.
stepsToPerform:
1. Open a new incognito browser window or clear all cookies and site data for the application's domain.
2. Navigate to the application's home page URL.
3. Observe that the page loads completely without any errors.
4. Verify that a modal, banner, or a distinct section for the 'short guided questionnaire' is prominently displayed on the page.
5. Confirm that the questionnaire is presented automatically, without requiring any user interaction like a button click.
6. Verify that no login, registration, or payment prompts appear before or along with the questionnaire.
7. Check that the underlying home page content remains visible or accessible around the questionnaire element.
expectedResult:
1. The guided questionnaire is automatically and prominently displayed on the home page for a first-time anonymous user.
2. The system correctly identifies the user as a new visitor and triggers the onboarding flow.
3. The user is not required to create an account or provide payment to see or interact with the questionnaire.

sourceCitation.excerpt: Collect the seeker's requirements through a short guided questionnaire offered from the home page on a first visit, before any account exists.

title: Verify an anonymous user can successfully complete the questionnaire by providing valid answers to all preference fields
description: This test validates the core 'happy path' for the preference capture feature, ensuring a user can submit a complete set of valid preferences. This is critical for the downstream job matching functionality to work as intended.
testDescription: An anonymous user interacts with the guided questionnaire, provides valid and realistic inputs for all available preference fields (e.g., working arrangement, salary, job titles), and successfully submits the form to receive personalized job matches.
prerequisites:
1. The user is anonymous and is presented with the guided questionnaire on the home page.
2. A set of valid test data for all preference fields is available.
3. The system has job listings that match the test data to ensure a non-empty results page.
stepsToPerform:
1. As a new anonymous user, navigate to the home page to trigger the questionnaire.
2. In the questionnaire, select 'fully remote' for the working arrangement.
3. Select 'income' as the motivation for the search.
4. Enter '120000' for the target annual salary.
5. Enter 'Senior Software Engineer' for the job title.
6. Select 'Information Technology' as the category.
7. Select '8+ years' for years of relevant experience.
8. Select 'Master's Degree' for the highest level of education.
9. Click the 'Submit' or 'See Your Matches' button to complete the questionnaire.
10. Observe that the system processes the inputs without any validation errors.
11. Verify that the user is redirected to the job matching results page.
expectedResult:
1. The system accepts all valid inputs without error.
2. Upon submission, the user's preferences are successfully saved to their anonymous session.
3. The user is navigated to a personalized job results page, with filters and rankings based on the submitted preferences.

sourceCitation.excerpt: The preferences captured cover: - the working arrangement sought (fully remote, hybrid, or no preference) - what is motivating the search...

title: Verify the system correctly records which preferences were provided and which were left unanswered when a user partially completes the questionnaire
description: This test verifies that the system correctly handles partial submissions, a common user behavior. It is important that the backend can distinguish between answered and unanswered fields to ensure matching logic is not skewed by default or null values.
testDescription: An anonymous user fills out some, but not all, of the preference fields in the questionnaire and submits it. The test will verify that the provided data is saved correctly and the skipped fields are explicitly recorded as unanswered.
prerequisites:
1. The user is an anonymous visitor presented with the guided questionnaire.
2. The system's backend session data or logs are accessible for verification during the test.
3. The questionnaire allows for submission even with some fields left blank.
stepsToPerform:
1. As a new anonymous user, navigate to the home page and begin the questionnaire.
2. For 'working arrangement', select 'hybrid'.
3. For 'job titles', enter 'Marketing Coordinator'.
4. Intentionally leave the 'annual salary the seeker is targeting' field blank.
5. Intentionally leave the 'years of relevant experience' selection unanswered.
6. Submit the questionnaire.
7. Verify the system accepts the partial submission and navigates to the job results page.
8. Using developer tools or backend access, inspect the user's anonymous session data.
9. Confirm that the values for 'working arrangement' and 'job titles' are stored correctly.
10. Confirm that the fields for 'annual salary' and 'years of experience' are stored as null, empty, or have a specific flag indicating they were unanswered.
expectedResult:
1. The system successfully processes the partially completed questionnaire without errors.
2. The preferences that were provided are correctly saved to the user's anonymous session.
3. The preferences that were left unanswered are correctly recorded as such, ensuring they do not influence the job matching results.

sourceCitation.excerpt: Record which preferences were provided and which were left unanswered.

title: Verify an anonymous user can revisit and change a previously submitted preference without having to repeat the entire questionnaire
description: This test ensures a user-friendly workflow for refining search preferences. Forcing a user to repeat the entire questionnaire to change one item would be a poor experience and could lead to abandonment.
testDescription: An anonymous user completes the questionnaire, views the initial job results, and then decides to change one of their preferences (e.g., from 'fully remote' to 'hybrid') to see a different set of results.
prerequisites:
1. The user is an anonymous visitor who has already completed and submitted the questionnaire in their current session.
2. The job results page provides a clear and accessible UI element to edit or revisit preferences.
3. The system contains jobs that would match both the initial and the changed preference.
stepsToPerform:
1. As a new anonymous user, complete the questionnaire, selecting 'fully remote' as the working arrangement, and submit it.
2. Verify you are on the job results page and the results are for remote roles.
3. Locate the UI element for editing preferences (e.g., a 'Refine Search' or 'Edit Preferences' button/link).
4. Click the element to open the preference editing interface.
5. Verify that an interface is presented that allows modification of individual preferences, not the full multi-step questionnaire.
6. In the editing interface, change the 'working arrangement' from 'fully remote' to 'hybrid'.
7. Save or apply the change.
8. Observe that the job results page refreshes or updates its content.
9. Verify the new job listings shown are relevant to the 'hybrid' preference.
10. Inspect the user's session data to confirm the preference value has been updated.
expectedResult:
1. The user can access an interface to change individual preferences directly from the results page.
2. The user is not forced to repeat the entire questionnaire to make a single change.
3. The updated preference is saved to the session, and the job results are correctly updated to reflect the change.

sourceCitation.excerpt: Allow preferences to be revisited and changed later without the seeker having to repeat the whole questionnaire.

title: Verify a user can enter a number of job titles up to the defined maximum limit
description: This is a boundary value test to ensure the system correctly handles the maximum allowed number of job titles. This prevents database errors or UI issues from an excessive number of entries. This test assumes the defined maximum is 5.
testDescription: A user interacting with the preference questionnaire enters exactly the maximum number of allowed job titles (e.g., 5) and successfully submits the form.
prerequisites:
1. The 'defined maximum' for job titles is configured to a known value (e.g., 5) in the test environment.
2. The user is an anonymous visitor interacting with the questionnaire.
stepsToPerform:
1. As a new anonymous user, start the questionnaire from the home page.
2. Navigate to the step for entering 'job titles'.
3. Enter the first job title: 'Product Manager'.
4. Enter the second job title: 'Project Manager'.
5. Enter the third job title: 'Scrum Master'.
6. Enter the fourth job title: 'Business Analyst'.
7. Enter the fifth and final allowed job title: 'Program Manager'.
8. Verify the UI has accepted all 5 entries.
9. Proceed to submit the questionnaire.
10. Verify the submission is successful and the user is taken to the job results page.
11. Inspect the session data to confirm all 5 job titles are correctly stored.
expectedResult:
1. The system accepts exactly the maximum defined number of job titles (5).
2. The user can successfully submit the form with the maximum number of titles.
3. All 5 entered titles are correctly saved and used for the subsequent job matching.

sourceCitation.excerpt: the job titles the seeker is targeting, up to a defined maximum

title: Verify a user is prevented from entering more job titles than the defined maximum limit
description: This is the negative boundary case for the job title limit, ensuring the system gracefully prevents users from exceeding the defined maximum. This protects system integrity and provides clear user feedback. This test assumes the defined maximum is 5.
testDescription: A user enters the maximum number of allowed job titles (5) and then attempts to add one more. The system should prevent the addition and display an informative message.
prerequisites:
1. The 'defined maximum' for job titles is configured to a known value (e.g., 5) in the test environment.
2. The user is an anonymous visitor interacting with the questionnaire.
stepsToPerform:
1. As a new anonymous user, start the questionnaire from the home page.
2. Navigate to the step for entering 'job titles'.
3. Successfully enter 5 distinct job titles.
4. Verify that the UI indicates the limit has been reached, for example, by disabling the 'Add' button or input field.
5. Attempt to type and add a sixth job title, 'Chief of Staff'.
6. Observe the UI's response.
7. Verify that the sixth job title cannot be added to the list of preferences.
8. Verify that a clear message is displayed, such as 'You have reached the maximum of 5 job titles.'
expectedResult:
1. The system strictly prevents the user from entering more than the maximum defined number of job titles.
2. A user-friendly message is displayed explaining the limit.
3. The UI for adding more titles is disabled or otherwise blocks input once the limit is reached.

sourceCitation.excerpt: the job titles the seeker is targeting, up to a defined maximum

title: Verify a user can successfully upload a resume in a common document format that is under the defined size limit
description: This test validates the core functionality of the resume upload feature. It ensures users can upload a correctly formatted and sized document, which is a critical prerequisite for many job applications. This test uses a .docx file under the size limit.
testDescription: An anonymous user, as part of the onboarding flow, uploads their resume. The file is a .docx document with a size of 2MB, which is a supported format and well under the typical size limit (e.g., 10MB).
prerequisites:
1. A test resume file in a supported format (e.g., `test_resume.docx`) is available for upload.
2. The test file's size (e.g., 2MB) is less than the system's configured maximum size limit.
3. The user is at the resume handling step of the onboarding questionnaire.
stepsToPerform:
1. As an anonymous user, proceed through the questionnaire to the resume handling step.
2. Click the 'Upload Resume' button or drag the file to the designated area.
3. When the file selection dialog appears, select the valid test file `test_resume.docx`.
4. Confirm the selection to initiate the upload.
5. Observe the UI for an upload progress indicator.
6. Wait for the upload process to complete.
7. Verify the upload completes without any error messages.
8. Confirm that a success message is displayed on the screen, indicating the document was received.
expectedResult:
1. The system accepts the resume file in the common .docx format.
2. The file is successfully uploaded and associated with the user's anonymous session.
3. The UI provides clear feedback to the user that the upload was successful.

sourceCitation.excerpt: Accept a resume upload in the common document formats, up to a defined size limit.

title: Verify the system provides a confirmation that an uploaded document has been received
description: This test verifies that the system provides explicit confirmation to the user after a resume upload. This feedback is crucial for user confidence, preventing duplicate uploads or uncertainty about whether the action was successful.
testDescription: After a user successfully uploads a resume document, the system should display a clear and immediate confirmation message on the UI, assuring the user that their document has been received and is ready for use.
prerequisites:
1. A valid test resume file (e.g., `my_cv.pdf`) is available for upload.
2. The user is on the resume upload screen within the onboarding flow.
stepsToPerform:
1. As an anonymous user, navigate to the resume handling step of the questionnaire.
2. Click the 'Upload Resume' button.
3. Select the valid test resume file `my_cv.pdf` and start the upload.
4. Wait for the upload to complete successfully.
5. Immediately observe the UI for changes.
6. Verify that a clear and unambiguous confirmation message is displayed, such as 'Success! Your resume "my_cv.pdf" has been uploaded.'
7. Verify the UI state changes to reflect the presence of the file, for example, by displaying the filename and providing an option to 'Replace' or 'Delete' it.
expectedResult:
1. An explicit confirmation message is displayed to the user immediately upon successful upload.
2. The UI is updated to show that a document has been received and is associated with the seeker's profile for the session.
3. The confirmation appears before the user navigates away from the page, ensuring they are aware of the successful action.

sourceCitation.excerpt: Confirm that an uploaded document has been received before it is treated as part of the seeker's profile.

title: Verify the system rejects a resume uploaded in an unsupported format and provides a clear reason for the rejection
description: This negative test ensures the system's file format validation is working correctly. It prevents the upload of unsupported or potentially malicious file types and provides helpful feedback to the user.
testDescription: A user attempts to upload a file in an unsupported format, such as an image file (.png). The system should reject the file and display a clear error message explaining which formats are acceptable.
prerequisites:
1. A test file in an unsupported format (e.g., `screenshot.png`) is available.
2. The list of supported formats is known (e.g., .pdf, .docx) and does not include .png.
3. The user is at the resume upload step.
stepsToPerform:
1. As an anonymous user, navigate to the resume handling step.
2. Click the 'Upload Resume' button.
3. In the file selection dialog, select the unsupported file `screenshot.png`.
4. Attempt to upload the selected file.
5. Observe the system's immediate response.
6. Verify that the upload is rejected either by the client-side validation or a server response.
7. Verify a clear and specific error message is displayed, such as 'Unsupported file type. Please upload your resume as a PDF or DOCX file.'
8. Confirm that no file is associated with the user's session.
expectedResult:
1. The system correctly identifies and rejects the file with an unsupported format.
2. A clear, user-friendly reason for the rejection is provided, guiding the user on corrective action.
3. The user's session remains without an associated resume file.

sourceCitation.excerpt: Reject unsupported formats and oversized documents with a clear reason.

title: Verify the system rejects a resume that exceeds the defined size limit and provides a clear reason for the rejection
description: This negative test ensures the file size limit is enforced, preventing users from uploading excessively large files that could strain system resources. It also confirms that clear feedback is provided to the user.
testDescription: A user attempts to upload a resume in a valid format (e.g., .pdf) but its file size exceeds the defined maximum limit (e.g., 10MB). The system should reject the upload and inform the user about the size constraint.
prerequisites:
1. A test resume file in a supported format (e.g., `large_portfolio.pdf`) with a size greater than the limit (e.g., 12MB) is available.
2. The maximum file size limit is configured in the test environment to 10MB.
stepsToPerform:
1. As an anonymous user, navigate to the resume handling step.
2. Click the 'Upload Resume' button.
3. From the file selection dialog, choose the oversized file `large_portfolio.pdf` (12MB).
4. Initiate the upload.
5. Observe the system's response as the file is processed.
6. Verify that the upload fails and is rejected by the system.
7. Confirm that a specific error message is displayed to the user, such as 'File is too large. Please upload a file smaller than 10MB.'
8. Verify that the oversized file is not saved or associated with the user's session.
expectedResult:
1. The system correctly rejects the file that exceeds the defined size limit.
2. A clear reason for the rejection, which includes the specific size limit, is provided to the user.
3. The user's session remains without an associated resume file.

sourceCitation.excerpt: Reject unsupported formats and oversized documents with a clear reason.

title: Verify a user can upload a resume with a file size exactly at the defined size limit
description: This test validates the system's handling of the upper boundary for file size, ensuring it correctly accepts a file that is exactly at the maximum allowed size without incorrectly rejecting it. Automation: HIGH.
testDescription: A new job seeker is completing the onboarding questionnaire and needs to upload their resume. They select a valid document file (e.g., .docx) that has been specifically created to be exactly the maximum size permitted by the system (e.g., 10MB). The test confirms the system processes this boundary case successfully.
prerequisites: The system must have a defined maximum file size limit for resume uploads (e.g., 10,240 KB). A test resume file in a supported format (.docx) with a size of exactly 10,240 KB must be available. The user is an anonymous visitor on the resume upload step of the onboarding process.
stepsToPerform:
1. As an anonymous user, navigate to the platform's home page.
2. Initiate the seeker preference questionnaire.
3. Proceed through the questionnaire to the 'Resume Handling' section.
4. Click the 'Upload Resume' button.
5. In the file selection dialog, choose the test resume file that is exactly at the size limit (10,240 KB).
6. Confirm the selection and initiate the upload.
7. Observe the system's feedback during and after the upload process.
8. Verify a success message like 'Resume uploaded successfully' is displayed on the screen.
9. Proceed to the next step of the questionnaire to ensure the process is not blocked.
expectedResult:
1. The resume file is successfully uploaded and accepted by the system.
2. A clear confirmation message is displayed to the user.
3. The system associates the uploaded resume with the user's current anonymous session.

sourceCitation.excerpt: Accept a resume upload in the common document formats, up to a defined size limit.

title: Verify a user can select their current resume state from the available options ('up to date', 'needs work', 'not written yet')
description: This test ensures the system correctly captures and stores the user's self-reported resume status, which is a key piece of profile information used to understand the seeker's readiness. Automation: HIGH.
testDescription: During the onboarding questionnaire, a new seeker is asked about the current state of their resume. The test verifies that the user can see all available options and that their selection is correctly registered by the system for their session.
prerequisites: User is a new, anonymous visitor. The user has started the onboarding questionnaire and has navigated to the 'Resume Handling' step.
stepsToPerform:
1. As an anonymous user, navigate to the platform's home page.
2. Start the guided questionnaire for new seekers.
3. Progress through the initial preference questions to reach the resume section.
4. Observe the question asking for the current state of the seeker's resume.
5. Verify that the three options are displayed: 'up to date', 'needs work', and 'not written yet'.
6. Select the 'needs work' option.
7. Proceed to the next step in the questionnaire.
8. Navigate back to the resume step.
9. Verify that the 'needs work' option is still selected, confirming the choice was saved in the session state.
expectedResult:
1. The user is able to select one of the three provided resume state options.
2. The system correctly captures the selected state ('needs work').
3. The selection is retained for the duration of the anonymous user's session.

sourceCitation.excerpt: Capture the current state of the seeker's resume (up to date, needs work, not written yet).

title: Verify a personalized set of job listings is produced, filtered, and ranked against the preferences captured from the user
description: This test validates the core job matching algorithm, ensuring that the preferences provided by a user directly translate into a correctly filtered and relevant set of job results. This is fundamental to the platform's value proposition. Automation: HIGH.
testDescription: A new anonymous seeker completes the onboarding questionnaire with a specific set of preferences (e.g., fully remote, >$120k salary, Software Engineering). The test verifies that the subsequent job listings page displays only jobs that meet these exact criteria.
prerequisites: The test database contains a mix of job listings: at least 5 jobs matching the test criteria, and at least 10 jobs that do not. Test criteria: Working Arrangement = 'fully remote', Target Salary >= '$120,000', Category = 'Software Engineering'. User is a new anonymous visitor.
stepsToPerform:
1. As an anonymous user, navigate to the home page.
2. Start the guided questionnaire.
3. For 'working arrangement', select 'fully remote'.
4. For 'annual salary', enter '120000'.
5. For 'category', select 'Software Engineering'.
6. Complete and submit the questionnaire.
7. The system should navigate to the job results page.
8. Inspect the first 5 job listings displayed.
9. For each listing, verify that the working arrangement is 'fully remote'.
10. For each listing, verify that the salary is >= $120,000 (or that it falls into a range consistent with this target).
11. For each listing, verify that it belongs to the 'Software Engineering' category.
expectedResult:
1. A list of job results is displayed to the user.
2. All displayed job listings strictly match the preferences captured in the questionnaire.
3. No jobs that fail to meet the specified criteria are shown on the first page of results.

sourceCitation.excerpt: Produce a personalised set of listings once the seeker's preferences have been captured, filtered and ranked against those preferences.

title: Verify a user can clear an individual preference filter from the job results page to widen the search
description: This test ensures that users can dynamically adjust their search criteria on the results page to explore more options, validating the 'clear filter' functionality for widening a search. Automation: HIGH.
testDescription: A seeker has a set of job results based on multiple preferences (e.g., location and salary). They decide the location preference is too restrictive and use an on-page control to clear it. The test verifies the job list updates to include jobs from other locations that were previously excluded.
prerequisites: User is on the job results page with at least two active filters (e.g., Location = 'United States' and Category = 'Marketing'). The test database contains 'Marketing' jobs both inside and outside the 'United States'.
stepsToPerform:
1. Start on the job results page with 'Location: United States' and 'Category: Marketing' filters active.
2. Note the initial number of job results displayed (e.g., 'Showing 25 jobs').
3. Locate the active filter display for 'Location: United States'.
4. Click the 'clear' or 'X' icon associated with the location filter.
5. Observe the job results list as it refreshes.
6. Verify that the 'Location' filter is no longer shown as active.
7. Verify that the new number of job results is greater than the initial count.
8. Inspect the new job listings to confirm that results from outside the 'United States' are now included.
expectedResult:
1. The job results list updates automatically without a full page reload.
2. The total number of results increases.
3. The cleared filter ('Location') is removed from the active filters list, while other filters ('Category') remain active.

sourceCitation.excerpt: Allow the seeker to widen, narrow or clear any individual preference from the results.

title: Verify a user can narrow the job results by modifying a preference directly on the results page
description: This test validates the 'narrow search' functionality, ensuring users can refine their job results by making their preferences more specific directly on the results page. Automation: HIGH.
testDescription: A seeker is viewing job results with a broad preference set (e.g., Experience Level: 'Any'). They use an on-page filter control to change this preference to 'Senior Level', expecting to see a smaller, more targeted list of jobs.
prerequisites: User is on the job results page with a broad filter applied (e.g., 'Years of relevant experience' is not set). The test database contains jobs that match other criteria at various experience levels (e.g., Entry, Mid, Senior).
stepsToPerform:
1. Start on the job results page with preferences applied, but without an experience level filter.
2. Note the initial number of job results displayed (e.g., 'Showing 150 jobs').
3. Locate the 'Years of relevant experience' filter control on the page.
4. Modify the filter to a more restrictive value (e.g., '10+ years').
5. Observe the job results list as it refreshes.
6. Verify that the 'Years of relevant experience' filter now shows the new value as active.
7. Verify that the new number of job results is less than the initial count.
8. Inspect the new job listings to confirm they match the '10+ years' experience requirement.
expectedResult:
1. The job results list updates automatically to reflect the new, narrower filter.
2. The total number of results decreases.
3. All jobs in the new list meet the more specific preference criteria.

sourceCitation.excerpt: Allow the seeker to widen, narrow or clear any individual preference from the results.

title: Verify the system indicates which specific constraint is narrowing the set when a combination of preferences returns very few listings
description: This test validates the user-assistance feature that helps seekers understand why their search results are limited, improving usability and preventing search abandonment. Automation: MEDIUM (requires UI element inspection).
testDescription: A seeker applies a combination of a common preference (e.g., Category: 'Sales') and a very niche preference (e.g., Workplace Benefit: 'On-site Pet Care'). This combination returns only one or two results. The test verifies that the system displays a message indicating that the 'Workplace Benefit' filter is the primary reason for the limited results.
prerequisites: The test database is configured so that a specific filter is highly restrictive. For example, many 'Sales' jobs exist, but only two also offer 'On-site Pet Care'. The threshold for 'very few' listings is defined (e.g., <= 3).
stepsToPerform:
1. As an anonymous user, start the guided questionnaire.
2. Select a common preference, 'Category: Sales'.
3. Select a very restrictive preference, 'Workplace benefit: On-site Pet Care'.
4. Complete the questionnaire and proceed to the job results page.
5. Verify that the number of results is very low (e.g., 'Showing 2 results').
6. Inspect the area around the active filter display.
7. Look for a specific UI indicator (e.g., a tooltip, highlight, or text message) associated with the 'Workplace benefit' filter.
8. Confirm the indicator's text suggests removing or changing this filter to see more results.
expectedResult:
1. The results page displays very few listings.
2. A clear visual indicator is displayed next to the 'Workplace benefit: On-site Pet Care' filter.
3. The message explicitly identifies this filter as the likely cause for the narrow result set.

sourceCitation.excerpt: Where a combination of preferences returns very few listings, indicate which constraint is narrowing the set.

title: Verify captured preferences are automatically applied to subsequent searches for the remainder of the anonymous visit
description: This test ensures that user preferences are maintained within a single session, providing a consistent experience and saving the user from re-entering their criteria repeatedly. Automation: HIGH.
testDescription: An anonymous seeker completes the questionnaire, gets a list of matched jobs, and then navigates back to the homepage to perform a new action, like a keyword search. The test verifies that the preferences from the questionnaire are still active and are applied as filters to this new search.
prerequisites: User is a new anonymous visitor. The session management is based on cookies or a similar mechanism.
stepsToPerform:
1. As an anonymous user, navigate to the home page.
2. Complete the guided questionnaire, setting 'working arrangement' to 'hybrid'.
3. View the initial job results and confirm the 'hybrid' filter is active.
4. Navigate back to the site's main home page using the site logo or navigation bar.
5. Locate the main keyword search bar on the home page.
6. Enter a generic job title like 'Manager' and submit the search.
7. On the new search results page, inspect the active filters.
8. Verify that the 'working arrangement: hybrid' filter is still applied to the 'Manager' search results.
9. Inspect the job listings to confirm they are for 'Manager' roles and are also 'hybrid'.
expectedResult:
1. The preferences captured via the questionnaire persist throughout the anonymous user's session.
2. When a new search is initiated, the persisted preferences are automatically applied as filters.
3. The user is not required to re-enter their core preferences during their visit.

sourceCitation.excerpt: Apply the captured preferences to subsequent searches for the remainder of the visit

title: Verify an anonymous user's preferences and resume are correctly carried over into their new account after completing registration triggered by saving a job
description: This critical end-to-end test verifies the integrity of the conversion funnel, ensuring all data captured from an anonymous user is seamlessly and accurately migrated to their new permanent account upon registration. Automation: HIGH.
testDescription: A new visitor completes the onboarding questionnaire, uploads their resume, views job matches, and then decides to save a job. This action prompts them to register. The test ensures their session data (all preferences and the resume file) is successfully associated with their new account after registration.
prerequisites: User must be a new, anonymous visitor. A valid resume file (e.g., resume_john_doe.pdf) must be available. At least one job listing exists. A unique email address (e.g., test+${uuid}@example.com) is available for registration.
stepsToPerform:
1. As a new anonymous user, navigate to the home page.
2. Complete the questionnaire with specific preferences: Location='Canada', Salary='95000', Category='Marketing'.
3. On the resume step, upload the 'resume_john_doe.pdf' file.
4. Proceed to the job results page and verify the results match the preferences.
5. Click the 'Save Job' icon on the first available job listing.
6. Verify the registration form is presented as a result of the action.
7. Complete the registration form with the unique email address and a password.
8. Submit the registration and complete any verification steps.
9. After being automatically logged in, navigate to the user's 'Account Profile' or 'My Preferences' page.
10. Verify the preferences are displayed correctly: Location='Canada', Salary='95000', Category='Marketing'.
11. Navigate to the 'My Resume' or 'Documents' section of the profile.
12. Verify the file 'resume_john_doe.pdf' is listed and associated with the account.
expectedResult:
1. The user is successfully registered and logged in.
2. All preferences captured during the anonymous session are present and correct in the new user's account settings.
3. The resume uploaded during the anonymous session is correctly associated with the new account.

sourceCitation.excerpt: Preferences captured before registration carry over into the account when the seeker signs up.

title: Verify the registration form is presented when an anonymous user with captured preferences attempts to apply for a job listing
description: This test verifies that the system correctly gates account-required actions and initiates the registration workflow at the 'Apply' trigger point. This validates the state transition from anonymous browsing to registration-required. Automation: HIGH.
testDescription: An anonymous seeker has completed the questionnaire and is browsing their personalized job results. They find a job they are interested in and click the 'Apply' button. The test confirms that this action correctly interrupts the flow and presents the registration/login page.
prerequisites: User is an anonymous visitor who has completed the preference questionnaire. The user is on the job results page viewing a list of matched jobs.
stepsToPerform:
1. As a new anonymous user, navigate to the home page.
2. Complete the guided questionnaire with any set of preferences.
3. On the job results page, observe the list of jobs.
4. Each job listing should have an 'Apply' button.
5. Click the 'Apply' button on the first job listing.
6. Observe the resulting page or modal dialog.
7. Verify that the content displayed is a registration form or a choice between 'Register' and 'Log In'.
8. Confirm that the user is not taken to an external application site or an internal application form.
expectedResult:
1. The system correctly intercepts the 'Apply' action for an anonymous user.
2. The user is presented with the registration form.
3. The application process is halted pending user registration or login.

sourceCitation.excerpt: Registration is requested only when the seeker acts on a listing — applying, saving it, or setting up alerts.

title: Verify an anonymous user can browse listings, complete the questionnaire, and view matched results without requiring an account or payment
description: This test verifies that the core value proposition of immediate, personalized job matching is accessible to new visitors without any barriers like registration or payment, which is critical for user engagement and reducing first-visit abandonment. Automation feasibility: HIGH.
testDescription: A new, anonymous visitor explores the job platform. The test ensures they can freely browse job listings, use the guided questionnaire to input their preferences, and see the resulting personalized job matches, all without being prompted to create an account or provide payment information.
prerequisites: User must be a new visitor with no existing session cookies for the site. The application's home page must be accessible. The job database must contain active listings.
stepsToPerform:
1. Open a new incognito/private browser window to ensure an anonymous session.
2. Navigate to the application's main home page. Observe that a guided questionnaire is offered.
3. Ignore the questionnaire and click on a general navigation link like 'Browse Jobs'. The page successfully loads a list of job listings.
4. Verify no login or payment prompt was shown. The user can view the job list.
5. Navigate back to the home page.
6. Complete the guided questionnaire with specific preferences (e.g., Working Arrangement: 'fully remote', Target Salary: '$100,000').
7. Submit the questionnaire. The system processes the request without any interruption for registration.
8. Observe the job matching results page is displayed.
9. Verify that the listings shown are filtered and ranked according to the preferences submitted in step 6.
10. Confirm that throughout this entire flow, the user was never required to log in, register, or pay.
expectedResult:
1. The anonymous user can successfully browse general job listings.
2. The user can complete the preference questionnaire and view personalized matched results.
3. At no point during browsing, completing the questionnaire, or viewing results is an account or payment required.

sourceCitation.excerpt: Browsing listings, completing the questionnaire and viewing matched results require no account and no payment.

title: Verify preferences and uploaded documents are held against the seeker for the duration of an anonymous visit
description: This test ensures that an anonymous user's session data is correctly maintained as they navigate the site, providing a consistent and uninterrupted job search experience. This is key to allowing them to explore without losing their personalized context. Automation feasibility: HIGH.
testDescription: An anonymous user fills out the preference questionnaire and uploads their resume. They then navigate to other parts of the website (e.g., blog, about us page) and then return to their job search. This test verifies that their preferences and resume are still associated with their session, and their search results remain personalized.
prerequisites: User must be a new, anonymous visitor. A valid test resume file (e.g., 'test_resume.pdf') must be available for upload. The application must be configured to use session-based storage for anonymous users.
stepsToPerform:
1. Start a new anonymous browser session and navigate to the home page.
2. Complete the guided questionnaire with specific preferences (e.g., Location: 'United States', Experience: '5+ years').
3. Proceed to the resume upload step and upload the 'test_resume.pdf' file. Observe a confirmation message that the upload was successful.
4. Submit the form and view the matched job results. Confirm the results are filtered by the entered preferences.
5. Navigate away from the results page to a non-functional page, such as the 'About Us' page.
6. Use the browser's back button or the site's main navigation to return to the job search results page.
7. Verify that the previously applied filters ('United States', '5+ years') are still active and the results are unchanged.
8. Navigate to a page where preferences can be edited. Confirm the fields are pre-populated with the data from step 2.
9. Verify there is an indicator that a resume ('test_resume.pdf') is currently associated with the session.
expectedResult:
1. All preferences entered by the anonymous user persist throughout their navigation within the same browser session.
2. The uploaded resume remains associated with the anonymous session.
3. Subsequent views of the job results page within the session automatically use the previously provided preferences and resume data.

sourceCitation.excerpt: Hold preferences and uploaded documents against the seeker for the duration of an anonymous visit

title: Verify preferences and uploaded documents are persisted against the user's account after registration is complete
description: This state-transition test validates the critical hand-off of data from an anonymous session to a newly created permanent account. A failure here would create a broken user experience and negate the value of the initial questionnaire. Automation feasibility: HIGH.
testDescription: A new visitor completes the onboarding questionnaire, uploads their resume, and views job matches. They then decide to save a job, which prompts them to register. The test ensures their session data is seamlessly and accurately migrated to their new permanent account upon successful registration.
prerequisites: User starts as an anonymous visitor. A valid test resume file (e.g., 'seeker_cv.docx') is available. A unique email address (e.g., 'test.seeker.123@example.com') is available for new account registration.
stepsToPerform:
1. Start a new anonymous browser session and navigate to the home page.
2. Complete the questionnaire with a unique set of preferences (e.g., Salary: '$95,000', Job Title: 'Product Manager', Benefit: 'Health Insurance').
3. Upload the 'seeker_cv.docx' resume file and observe the confirmation message.
4. Proceed to the matched job results page.
5. Click the 'Save Job' button on the first listing. Observe that a registration form is displayed.
6. Complete the registration form using the email 'test.seeker.123@example.com' and a valid password.
7. Submit the registration form. The user is now logged into their new account.
8. Navigate to the 'Account Profile' or 'My Preferences' section of the site.
9. Verify that the preferences from step 2 ('$95,000', 'Product Manager', 'Health Insurance') are correctly displayed in the user's profile.
10. Verify that the 'seeker_cv.docx' resume is listed as the user's current resume on file.
expectedResult:
1. The user's state successfully transitions from anonymous to registered.
2. All preferences captured during the anonymous session are correctly saved to the new user account without any data loss.
3. The resume uploaded during the anonymous session is correctly associated with the new user account.

sourceCitation.excerpt: Preferences captured before registration carry over into the account when the seeker signs up.

title: Verify a retained resume is used in the job matching process for a registered user on subsequent visits
description: This test confirms that once a user has an account with a resume, the system leverages that data for future job matching, enhancing the personalization of their experience on return visits. Automation feasibility: HIGH.
testDescription: A registered user who has previously uploaded a resume with specific, unique keywords logs into the platform. Without performing an explicit keyword search, the test verifies that the system proactively suggests jobs that are a good match for the content of their resume.
prerequisites: A registered user account exists with a specific resume already uploaded. The resume contains unique keywords (e.g., 'Quantum Computing', 'PMP Certified'). The job database contains listings that match these keywords. The user is logged out.
stepsToPerform:
1. Navigate to the application's login page.
2. Log in with the credentials of the pre-existing registered user.
3. Navigate to the user's profile page and confirm that the specific resume is on file.
4. Navigate to the main job search or dashboard page without entering any new search criteria.
5. The system should automatically generate a list of recommended or matched jobs.
6. Examine the top results displayed on the page.
7. Verify that job listings containing the unique keywords from the resume (e.g., 'Quantum Computing', 'PMP Certified') are present and ranked highly in the results.
8. Log out of the account.
9. Log back in to begin a new session.
10. Navigate again to the job search page and verify that the resume-based matching is still being applied.
expectedResult:
1. The system correctly uses the registered user's stored resume to inform the job matching algorithm.
2. Job listings that align with the content and keywords of the user's resume are included in the search results.
3. This personalized matching behavior persists across multiple login sessions for the registered user.

sourceCitation.excerpt: Retain the resume against the seeker for use in matching and in any applications they go on to make.

title: Verify a registered user can successfully remove their uploaded resume from their account profile
description: This test validates a user's right to data control by ensuring they can easily remove their Personally Identifiable Information (resume) from the platform. This is a key functional and data privacy requirement. Automation feasibility: HIGH.
testDescription: A registered user with an existing resume on their profile decides to remove it. The test walks through the process of navigating to their profile, initiating the deletion, confirming the action, and verifying that the resume is permanently disassociated from their account.
prerequisites: A registered user account exists. The account has a resume file (e.g., 'my_old_resume.pdf') uploaded and associated with it. The user is not logged in.
stepsToPerform:
1. Navigate to the application's login page.
2. Log in using the credentials of the prepared user account.
3. Navigate to the 'Account Profile' or 'My Documents' section.
4. Verify that the resume 'my_old_resume.pdf' is displayed as the current resume.
5. Locate and click the 'Remove Resume' or 'Delete' button associated with the resume file.
6. A confirmation modal appears asking 'Are you sure you want to remove your resume?'.
7. Click the 'Confirm' button on the modal.
8. The page refreshes, and an indicator (e.g., 'No resume uploaded') is now displayed where the resume file was.
9. Log out of the account.
10. Log back into the account to start a new session.
11. Navigate back to the 'Account Profile' section.
12. Verify that the resume is still gone and the 'No resume uploaded' state has persisted.
expectedResult:
1. The user is able to successfully initiate and confirm the resume removal process from their account settings.
2. After confirmation, the resume file is no longer associated with their account.
3. The removal of the resume is a permanent change that persists across sessions.

sourceCitation.excerpt: Allow the seeker to remove their resume and clear their preferences.

title: Verify a registered user can successfully clear all of their saved job preferences from their account
description: This test validates the user's ability to reset their search criteria, allowing them to start a new job search with a clean slate. This supports the requirement for user control over their data and profile personalization. Automation feasibility: HIGH.
testDescription: A registered user has previously saved a specific set of job preferences. The user now wishes to reset their search. This test verifies they can find and use a 'Clear All' function to remove all saved preferences from their account.
prerequisites: A registered user account exists. The account has multiple job preferences saved (e.g., Working Arrangement: 'hybrid', Salary: '> $80,000', Category: 'Sales'). The user is not logged in.
stepsToPerform:
1. Navigate to the application's login page.
2. Log in with the credentials of the prepared user account.
3. Navigate to the 'My Preferences' or 'Search Settings' page.
4. Verify that the previously saved preferences ('hybrid', '> $80,000', 'Sales') are displayed and active.
5. Locate and click the 'Clear All Preferences' or 'Reset Filters' button.
6. A confirmation dialog appears asking 'Are you sure you want to clear all your preferences?'.
7. Click 'Confirm' on the dialog.
8. The page refreshes, and all preference fields are now empty or reset to their default 'Any' state.
9. Log out of the account.
10. Log back into the account to start a new session.
11. Navigate back to the 'My Preferences' page.
12. Verify that all preferences remain cleared and have not reverted to their previous values.
expectedResult:
1. The user can successfully use a function to clear all saved job preferences.
2. After confirmation, all previously saved preferences are removed from the user's account.
3. The cleared preference state is persistent across login sessions.

sourceCitation.excerpt: Allow the seeker to remove their resume and clear their preferences.

title: Verify that after a user clears their preferences, subsequent job searches no longer apply the previously saved filters
description: This end-to-end test ensures that clearing preferences has the intended functional impact on the job matching system. It validates that the data removal action correctly influences downstream system behavior, providing an unfiltered search experience. Automation feasibility: HIGH.
testDescription: A user with very specific, restrictive saved preferences first performs a search to confirm the filters are working. They then clear all preferences and perform the search again, verifying that the results are now broad and unfiltered.
prerequisites: A registered user account exists with specific, restrictive preferences saved (e.g., Location: 'Antarctica', Job Title: 'Penguin Scientist'). The job database has jobs that match these criteria and many other jobs that do not. The user is logged out.
stepsToPerform:
1. Log in with the prepared user account credentials.
2. Navigate to the main job search page.
3. Verify that the search results are automatically and narrowly filtered by the saved preferences, showing only 'Penguin Scientist' roles in 'Antarctica'.
4. Navigate to the 'My Preferences' page.
5. Use the 'Clear All Preferences' function and confirm the action.
6. Verify the preference fields on the page are now empty or set to their default values.
7. Navigate back to the main job search page.
8. Observe the new search results. The list of jobs should now be much larger and more diverse.
9. Verify that jobs outside the original 'Antarctica' and 'Penguin Scientist' criteria are now visible in the results.
10. Refresh the page and confirm the search results remain broad and unfiltered.
expectedResult:
1. Before clearing, job searches are correctly filtered by the user's saved preferences.
2. After the user clears their preferences, subsequent job searches are no longer filtered by the old criteria.
3. The job results page displays a broad, unfiltered set of listings, correctly reflecting the cleared preference state.

sourceCitation.excerpt: Allow the seeker to remove their resume and clear their preferences.
